Bangkok's street food scene is one of the best reasons to visit the city, and no trip is complete without wandering the night markets in search of the next great bite. Read more in our companion piece, [Best Beaches in Portugal](/other-article), for a very different kind of trip.

<iframe src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ" title="Bangkok street food tour" width="560" height="315"></iframe>

![A vendor grilling skewers at a Bangkok night market](/placeholder.svg)

Here's what to look for when you're picking a stall:

- Signs of a good vendor
  - A long line of locals, not just tourists
  - A small, focused menu
  - High turnover of fresh ingredients
- Dishes worth seeking out
  - Pad kra pao (holy basil stir-fry)
  - Moo ping (grilled pork skewers)
  - Khao soi (northern-style curry noodles)

Once you've found a stall you trust, go back for seconds — the best vendors sell out early, so timing your visit matters as much as picking the right dish.
